questions: Which capital decisions actually create the catastrophic peak-to-trough losses, and how much lifetime alpha do those same decisions create?
Given a correctly identified crash onset, can a blind fixed-duration exit/reentry rule based only on prior crash durations avoid substantial downside without requiring bottom detection?

classifications: pre-peak holding vs entered after peak
eventual terminal winner vs terminal loser
metrics: share of peak-to-trough dollar loss by class
share of lifetime terminal-return mass by implicated trade set
concentration of loss in worst 5% and 10% of trade contributions

fixed_timeout.purpose: management ceiling test, not detector test
fixed_timeout.duration_estimation: for each crash, use trading-session onset-to-trough durations of the other three crashes only
fixed_timeout.action: one-shot liquidate all active positions at trigger close; suppress new entries for timeout sessions; then resume ordinary MTS automatically; no bottom/stabilization condition

prohibitions: no tuning of timeout beyond frozen mean/median
